name: Linear regression

subjectOf.text: In simple linear regressions of monthly returns on log AUM across the full sample, the AUM coefficient is statistically significant at the 5 percent level only during March through August 2012.
subjectOf.abstract: When considering the entire sample and no dummy variable, the estimated beta for the logarithm of the AUM are statistically significant at 5% level only in the period March-August 2012.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416

subjectOf.text: In the period close to and following the registration effective date, fund size has a positive relationship with fund performance, with positive beta coefficients in March through May and July 2012.
subjectOf.abstract: In the period close to and following the registration effective date for hedge fund advisers under the Dodd-Frank Act, the size of funds seems to have a positive relationship with the fund performance.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: coefficients negative in June and August 2012

subjectOf.text: Adding a dummy for AUM above $150 million to the linear regressions leaves no variable significant at the 5 percent level in March 2012, and the dummy is significant only in April 2012.
subjectOf.abstract: We notice that in March 2012, no variable is statistically significant at 5% significance level while in April 2012, the dummy variable is statistically significant.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: linear model with AUM threshold dummy

subjectOf.text: The linear regression models are jointly valid on the F-statistic but their explanatory power measured by R-squared remains very limited, with R-squared values of roughly 0.003 to 0.014.
subjectOf.abstract: The F-statistics support the validity of the models, while the explanatory power, measured by the R-squared is still very limited.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: linear models with and without the AUM dummy

subjectOf.text: In simple linear regressions of monthly returns on log AUM across December 2011 to December 2012, fund size does not appear to matter for fund returns because only a few coefficients are statistically significant and those remain close to zero.
subjectOf.abstract: We conclude that size of the funds in our sample does not appear to matter for fund returns as only a few coefficients are statistically significant but are still close to zero.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2816408
scope_conditions: monthly cross sections December 2011 to December 2012

subjectOf.text: Fund size shows a negative relationship with performance in the months before the March 2012 registration effective date and a positive relationship afterward, with beta coefficients negative in January to March 2012 and July 2012 and positive in April and May 2012.
subjectOf.abstract: Examining the beta coefficients, we notice that in the period January - March 2012 and July 2012, beta coefficients are negative, while immediately after the registration effective date, e.g. April-May 2012 the beta coefficient is positive.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2816408
scope_conditions: monthly linear regressions, December 2011 to December 2012

subjectOf.text: In regressions including a dummy for AUM above $150 million, the dummy is statistically significant and positive only in April and September 2012, and the explanatory power of the models measured by R-squared remains very limited.
subjectOf.abstract: The dummy variables are statistically significant and positive in April and September 2012. The F-statistics support the validity of the models, while the explanatory power, measured by the R- squared is still very limited.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2816408
scope_conditions: linear models with dummy, December 2011 to December 2012
